instruction: Identify the mountains in three photos from the Pictures folder, create folders named after each mountain, and move each photo into its respective folder.

metadata.explanation: Task requires identifying 3 mountain images and organizing them into folders named after the mountains (Kilimanjaro, Everest, Mount Hua/Huashan). The evaluator checks that folders with mountain keywords exist and each contains at least 1 file. Verified: picture1.jpg=Kilimanjaro (iconic snow-capped peak with moon and savanna), picture2.jpg=Everest (highest peak with rugged Himalayan terrain), picture3.jpg=Mount Hua (Chinese mountain with famous plank walk). Similar complexity to original task (identify + file operation) but requires creating folders instead of renaming.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements through 3 comprehensive checks
Check 1 (lines 30-37 in metric): Verifies original files were MOVED not copied by confirming picture1.jpg, picture2.jpg, picture3.jpg no longer exist in base /home/user/Pictures/ directory
Check 2 (lines 39-53 in metric): Verifies folders with mountain keywords (kilimanjaro, everest, hua) exist and contain at least the expected file count

Check 3 (lines 55-70 in metric): Verifies correct picture-to-folder mapping by checking each picture is in the folder containing the expected mountain keyword (picture1.jpg in kilimanjaro folder, picture2.jpg in everest folder, picture3.jpg in hua folder)
Getter correctly extracts both folder structure with file lists and original file existence status, providing all data needed for verification
Expected values are semantically correct and match the mountain identification metadata
Minor issue: Metric uses >= for file count comparison (line 46), allowing extra unrelated files to pass, but this is not critical for the task
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using exact equality (==) instead of >= for file count comparison if strict verification is needed
